operations.title: Get account balance
operations.doc: Returns the balance of a single account for the given date.

params.name: id
params.doc: The ID of the account.

params.name: date
params.doc: The date for the balance (always end of day). Defaults to the last day of the current fiscal period. See Switch fiscal period. Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Example: 2020-01-15.

operations.title: Create bank account
operations.doc: Creates a new bank account. Returns either a success or multiple error messages (for each issue).

params.name: bic
params.doc: The BIC (Business Identifier Code) of your bank.

params.name: iban
params.doc: The IBAN (International Bank Account Number).

params.name: name
params.doc: The name of the bank account. This can contain localized text. To add values in multiple languages, use the XML format like this: <values><de>German text</de><en>English text</en></values>

params.name: type
params.doc: The type of bank account, i.e. what is the bank account used for?

params.name: accountId
params.doc: The ID of the financial account linked to this bank account. See Account.

params.name: attachments
params.doc: List of files to attach. This is a JSON array [{...},{...},...] with the following parameters:

sub.name: fileId
sub.doc: ID of the file to attach. See File.

params.name: currencyId
params.doc: The ID of the currency. Leave empty to use the default currency. See Currency.

params.name: isInactive
params.doc: Mark this bank account as inactive. Inactive bank accounts are greyed out in the list and are no longer suggested by the app.

params.name: notes
params.doc: Some optional notes. This can contain limited HTML for styling. Allowed tags: a, p, div, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, ul, ol, li, blockquote, b, i, s, u, o, sup, sub, ins, del, strong, strike, tt, code, big, small, br, span, em. Allowed inline CSS rules: background, background-color, color, font, font-size, font-weight, font-style, text-align, text-indent, text-decoration.

params.name: qrFirstDigits
params.doc: The first few digits of the Swiss QR reference (0 by default). This is specific to Switzerland.

params.name: qrIban
params.doc: The QR-IBAN, which is an IBAN especially for QR invoices (former ESR). This is specific to Switzerland.

params.name: url
params.doc: An optional URL for the bank's e-banking portal.

operations.title: Update account
operations.doc: Updates an existing account. Note that all parameters must be submitted, omitted parameters are treated as empty values. Returns either a success or multiple error messages (for each issue).

params.name: categoryId
params.doc: The ID of the category. See Account category.

params.name: id
params.doc: The ID of the account to update.

params.name: name
params.doc: The name of the account. This can contain localized text. To add values in multiple languages, use the XML format like this: <values><de>German text</de><en>English text</en></values>

params.name: number
params.doc: The account number. Must be numeric but can contain a decimal point.

params.name: allocations
params.doc: Allocations to cost centers, if this account is either an expense or revenue account. This is a JSON array [{...},{...},...] with the following parameters:

sub.name: share
sub.doc: Allocation share. For example, if you have two cost centers, and one has a share of 3, and the other has a share of 1, then the amount is allocated 3:1 (which equals 75% to 25%).

sub.name: toCostCenterId
sub.doc: ID of cost center to allocate to. See Cost center.

params.name: attachments
params.doc: List of files to attach. This is a JSON array [{...},{...},...] with the following parameters:

sub.name: fileId
sub.doc: ID of the file to attach. See File.

params.name: currencyId
params.doc: The ID of the account's currency. Leave empty to use the default currency. See Currency.

params.name: custom
params.doc: Custom field values. They are stored as XML in this parameter. Example: <values><customField1>My value</customField1><customField2>["value 1","value 2"]</customField2></values>. Look up custom field variable names (e.g. "customField1") in the Custom fields API.

params.name: isInactive
params.doc: Mark this account as inactive. Inactive accounts are greyed out in the list and are no longer suggested.

params.name: notes
params.doc: Some optional notes. This can contain limited HTML for styling. Allowed tags: a, p, div, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, ul, ol, li, blockquote, b, i, s, u, o, sup, sub, ins, del, strong, strike, tt, code, big, small, br, span, em. Allowed inline CSS rules: background, background-color, color, font, font-size, font-weight, font-style, text-align, text-indent, text-decoration.

params.name: targetMax
params.doc: The target maximum balance (aka budget) you hope this account to stay beneath of by the end of the fiscal period. This will then be displayed by the Targets report, comparing your target to the actual balance. Please first switch to the desired fiscal period to set the target for that period, see Switch fiscal period.

params.name: targetMin
params.doc: The target minimum balance you hope this account to hit by the end of the fiscal period. This will then be displayed by the Targets report, comparing your target to the actual balance. Please first switch to the desired fiscal period to set the target for that period, see Switch fiscal period.

params.name: taxId
params.doc: The ID of the tax code associated with this account. See Tax codes.

operations.title: Update attachments

params.name: id
params.doc: The ID of the entry.

params.name: fileIds
params.doc: A list of file IDs, comma-separated. Leave empty to remove all attachments. Use the File API to upload a file and then use the file ID here.

operations.title: Create currency
operations.doc: Creates a new currency. The currency code must be unique. Returns either a success or multiple error messages (for each issue).

params.name: code
params.doc: The 3-characters currency code, like CHF, EUR, etc.

params.name: description
params.doc: An optional description of the currency. This can contain localized text. To add values in multiple languages, use the XML format like this: <values><de>German text</de><en>English text</en></values>

params.name: isDefault
params.doc: Use the currency as the default / main currency. This can only be set if there are no book entries yet. Defaults to false.

params.name: rate
params.doc: The exchange rate of this currency into the default currency. If this currency is the default currency, then the rate is 1. For most currencies, CashCtrl automatically retrieves the exchange rate, so this doesn't have to be set and will be ignored. Only set the rate for unsupported currencies. For supported currencies, see Get exchange rate.

operations.title: Delete currencies
operations.doc: Deletes one or multiple currencies. Only unused currencies can be deleted, and the main currency cannot be deleted (switch first). Returns either a success or error message.

params.name: ids
params.doc: The IDs of the selected entries, comma-separated.

operations.title: Get exchange rate
operations.doc: Returns the exchange rate between two currencies for a specific date.

params.name: from
params.doc: The source currency to convert.

params.name: to
params.doc: The target currency to convert into.

params.name: date
params.doc: The date for the exchange rate. Leave empty to use today. Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Example: 2020-01-15.

operations.doc: Creates a new custom field for the given type. Returns either a success or multiple error messages (for each issue).

params.name: dataType
params.doc: The data type of the custom field.

params.name: rowLabel
params.doc: Label displayed left of the field. If multiple custom fields have the same rowLabel, they will be displayed on the same row. This can contain localized text. To add values in multiple languages, use the XML format like this: <values><de>German text</de><en>English text</en></values>

params.name: type
params.doc: The type of custom field, meaning: which module the custom field belongs to.

params.name: fieldInfo
params.doc: An optional description of the custom field (displayed by hovering over an info icon). This can contain localized text. To add values in multiple languages, use the XML format like this: <values><de>German text</de><en>English text</en></values>

params.name: fieldLabel
params.doc: Smaller label displayed above the field. This can contain localized text. To add values in multiple languages, use the XML format like this: <values><de>German text</de><en>English text</en></values>

params.name: fieldTextRight
params.doc: Optional text displayed right of the field. This can contain localized text. To add values in multiple languages, use the XML format like this: <values><de>German text</de><en>English text</en></values>

params.name: groupId
params.doc: The ID of the custom field group. If empty, the custom field is in the default group 'More'. Groups are basically displayed as tabs in the edit dialog, whereas the default tab is 'More'.

params.name: isInactive
params.doc: Mark the custom field as inactive. Inactive custom fields are no longer displayed anywhere. However, the data is not removed, as opposed to deleting the custom field. Defaults to false.

params.name: isMulti
params.doc: Is the custom field a multi-field? Multi-fields can have multiple values. The data is then stored as JSON array, like for example ["val1", "val2", "val3"]. Defaults to false.

params.name: maxWidth
params.doc: The maximum width of the field. By default, the field width is stretched.

params.name: values
params.doc: Values the user can choose from, if the data type is COMBOBOX. Ignored otherwise. Use the JSON format like this: ["red","green","blue"]. Note that these values are not enforced, the user can still set arbitrary text as the custom field value.

params.name: variableName
params.doc: An optional, more meaningful variable name, instead of the default $customField variable name. Must start with a $ and contain only alphanumeric characters.

sub.doc: Text to filter by, or a JSON array of multiple values (OR).

params.name: limit
params.doc: The number of entries to retrieve. Defaults to 100.

params.name: mimeTypes
params.doc: Filter the file list by these mime types (comma-separated). For example, use image/* to filter by images only.

params.name: onlyNotes
params.doc: Flag to only include entries with notes. Defaults to false.

params.name: onlyWithoutCategory
params.doc: Flag to include only files without a category. Defaults to false.

params.name: query
params.doc: Fulltext search query.

params.name: sort
params.doc: The column to sort the list by. Defaults to 'lastUpdated'.

params.name: start
params.doc: The starting entry. Defaults to 0.

params.name: withoutSub
params.doc: Flag to exclude files in sub-categories. Defaults to false.

operations.title: Persist files
operations.doc: Persists one or multiple temporary files that have been prepared and uploaded. See Prepare files endpoint.

params.name: ids
params.doc: The IDs of the selected entries, comma-separated.

operations.title: Prepare files
operations.doc: Prepares one or multiple files for uploading. This is the starting point for uploading files to CashCtrl. In this step, you only provide file metadata, not the actual file. Returns a list of file IDs and write URLs. Use the write URL to upload the file binary (using the PUT method). See the Examples for a tutorial on how to upload a file (prepare put persist).

params.name: files
params.doc: The files to prepare. This is a JSON array [{...},{...},...] with the following parameters:

sub.name: mimeType
sub.doc: The mime type (content type) of the file. E.g. "application/pdf" for PDFs.

sub.name: name
sub.doc: The file name. Must be a valid file name, but doesn't have to be unique.

sub.name: categoryId
sub.doc: The ID of the category to add the file in.

sub.name: size
sub.doc: The size of the file. This helps to determine early if the storage quota is exceeded or not. However, the actual file size will be determined later upon persisting the file.

operations.title: Read file metadata
operations.doc: Returns the metadata of a single file by ID. Does not contain the file binary.

params.name: id
params.doc: The ID of the entry.

operations.title: Restore files
operations.doc: Restores one or multiple files that have been archived (moved to recycle bin). Returns either a success or error message.

params.name: ids
params.doc: The IDs of the selected entries, comma-separated.

operations.title: Update file
operations.doc: Updates an existing file (only metadata, not binary). Note that all parameters must be submitted, omitted parameters are treated as empty values. Returns either a success or multiple error messages (for each issue).

params.name: id
params.doc: The ID of the file to update.

params.name: name
params.doc: The file name.

params.name: categoryId
params.doc: The ID of the category. See File category.

params.name: custom
params.doc: Custom field values. They are stored as XML in this parameter. Example: <values><customField1>My value</customField1><customField2>["value 1","value 2"]</customField2></values>. Look up custom field variable names (e.g. "customField1") in the Custom fields API.

params.name: description
params.doc: A description for the file. This can contain localized text. To add values in multiple languages, use the XML format like this: <values><de>German text</de><en>English text</en></values>

params.name: notes
params.doc: Some optional notes. This can contain limited HTML for styling. Allowed tags: a, p, div, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, ul, ol, li, blockquote, b, i, s, u, o, sup, sub, ins, del, strong, strike, tt, code, big, small, br, span, em. Allowed inline CSS rules: background, background-color, color, font, font-size, font-weight, font-style, text-align, text-indent, text-decoration.

params.name: replaceWith
params.doc: Optionally replace the file binary (contents) with the binary from another file. Set the file ID here. That file must be a temporary file (not persisted yet). See Prepare files endpoint.

operations.title: Book depreciations
operations.doc: Book depreciations on fixed assets in the current fiscal period (see Switch fiscal period).

params.name: depreciation
params.doc: The IDs of fixed asset accounts to depreciate, comma-separated. See previous endpoint for a list of depreciable accounts.

params.name: id
params.doc: The ID of the fiscal period.

operations.title: Book currency exchange differences
operations.doc: Book currency exchange differences in the current fiscal period (see Switch fiscal period). These book entries make corrections to the main currency balance of accounts with a foreign currency.

params.name: exchangeDiff
params.doc: The exchange differences to book. This is a JSON array [{...},{...},...] with the following parameters:

sub.name: accountId
sub.doc: The ID of the account in a foreign currency.

sub.name: currencyRate
sub.doc: The final exchange rate to use (by which the main currency amount will be corrected).

params.name: date
params.doc: The booking date. Leave empty to use the last day of the fiscal period. If date is set, the fiscal period ID is ignored. Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Example: 2020-01-15.

params.name: id
params.doc: The ID of the fiscal period. Set either this or the date.

operations.title: Complete fiscal period
operations.doc: Completes the fiscal period. This action locks the book entries in this period so they cannot be manipulated anymore. However, you can reopen the fiscal period any time, see next API endpoint.

params.name: id
params.doc: The ID of the fiscal period to complete.

params.name: isSalary
params.doc: Complete the salary period instead of the fiscal period? Defaults to false.

operations.title: Complete months
operations.doc: Completes the given months. This action locks the book entries in this period so they cannot be manipulated anymore. However, you can reopen those months any time, see next API endpoint.

params.name: id
params.doc: The ID of the fiscal period to update.

params.name: isSalary
params.doc: Update the months for the salary period instead of the fiscal period? Defaults to false.

params.name: months
params.doc: List of months to close and protect from changes. As as consequence, all other months not listed here within the same fiscal period stay open or become reopened. This is a JSON array of month identifiers. Example month identifier: "2022-03". Example array: ["2022-01", "2022-02", "2022-03"] = This would close Jan,Feb,Mar of 2022, but leave Apr,May,Jun,Jul,Aug,Sep,Oct,Nov open.

operations.title: Create fiscal period
operations.doc: Creates a new manual fiscal period. Returns either a success or multiple error messages (for each issue).

params.name: end
params.doc: The end date of the fiscal period, if isCustom is set to true, ignored otherwise. Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Example: 2020-01-15.

params.name: isCustom
params.doc: If true, create a custom fiscal period with start and end date. type will be ignored. Defaults to false.

params.name: name
params.doc: The name of the fiscal period, if isCustom is set to true, ignored otherwise.

params.name: salaryEnd
params.doc: The end date of the salary period, if isCustom is set to true, ignored otherwise. Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Example: 2020-01-15.

params.name: salaryStart
params.doc: The start date of the salary period, if isCustom is set to true, ignored otherwise. Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Example: 2020-01-15.

params.name: start
params.doc: The start date of the fiscal period, if isCustom is set to true, ignored otherwise. Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Example: 2020-01-15.

params.name: type
params.doc: Creation type for creating a calendar year, if isCustom is not set. Either LATEST, which will create the next year after the latest existing year, or EARLIEST, which will create the year before the earliest existing year. Defaults to LATEST.

operations.title: Delete fiscal periods
operations.doc: Deletes one or multiple fiscal periods. Note that you cannot delete fiscal periods if there are book entries that are not covered by another fiscal period. Returns either a success or error message.

params.name: ids
params.doc: The IDs of the selected entries, comma-separated.

operations.title: List depreciations
operations.doc: List the depreciations on fixed assets to be booked in the current fiscal period (see Switch fiscal period). This doesn't actually book anything, see the next API endpoint for that.

params.name: id
params.doc: The ID of the entry.

operations.title: List currency exchange differences
operations.doc: List the currency exchange differences to be booked in the current fiscal period (see Switch fiscal period). These book entries make corrections to the main currency balance of accounts with a foreign currency. This doesn't actually book anything, see the next API endpoint for that.

params.name: date
params.doc: The booking date. Leave empty to use the last day of the fiscal period. If date is set, the fiscal period ID is ignored. Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Example: 2020-01-15.

params.name: id
params.doc: The ID of the fiscal period. Set either this or the date.

operations.title: List fiscal periods
operations.doc: Returns a list of all fiscal periods.

operations.title: Read fiscal period
operations.doc: Returns a single fiscal period by ID or the current fiscal period.

params.name: id
params.doc: The ID of the fiscal period. Leave empty to read the current fiscal period (see Switch fiscal period).

operations.title: Reopen fiscal period
operations.doc: Reopens the fiscal period. This unlocks the book entries in this period so they can be manipulated again.

params.name: id
params.doc: The ID of the fiscal period to reopen.

params.name: isSalary
params.doc: Complete the salary period instead of the fiscal period? Defaults to false.

operations.title: Reopen months
operations.doc: Reopens the given months. This unlocks the book entries in this period so they can be manipulated again.

params.name: id
params.doc: The ID of the fiscal period to update.

params.name: isSalary
params.doc: Update the months for the salary period instead of the fiscal period? Defaults to false.

This is a JSON array of month identifiers. Example month identifier: "2022-03". Example array: ["2022-01", "2022-02", "2022-03"] = This would close Jan,Feb,Mar of 2022, but leave Apr,May,Jun,Jul,Aug,Sep,Oct,Nov open.

operations.title: Get result
operations.doc: Get the result (profit or loss) of the given fiscal period.

params.name: id
params.doc: The ID of the fiscal period.

operations.title: Switch fiscal period
operations.doc: Switches the current fiscal period. Every user has a current fiscal period set, which is considered for various data responses like e.g. the list of journal entries. If you retrieve the list of journal entries, only the entries in the current fiscal period are returned. You have to use this API endpoint to switch the current fiscal period to another one.

params.name: id
params.doc: The ID of the entry.

operations.title: Create task
operations.doc: Creates a new task. Returns either a success or error message.

params.name: name
params.doc: The name/text of the task.

operations.title: Delete tasks
operations.doc: Deletes one or multiple tasks. Returns either a success or error message.

params.doc: The IDs of the selected entries, comma-separated.

params.name: id
params.doc: The ID of the fiscal period to update.

params.name: end
params.doc: The end date of the fiscal period, if isCustom is set to true, ignored otherwise. Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Example: 2020-01-15.

params.name: isCustom
params.doc: If true, create a custom fiscal period with start and end date. type will be ignored. Defaults to false.

params.name: name
params.doc: The name of the fiscal period, if isCustom is set to true, ignored otherwise.

params.name: salaryEnd
params.doc: The end date of the salary period, if isCustom is set to true, ignored otherwise. Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Example: 2020-01-15.

params.name: salaryStart
params.doc: The start date of the salary period, if isCustom is set to true, ignored otherwise. Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Example: 2020-01-15.

params.name: start
params.doc: The start date of the fiscal period, if isCustom is set to true, ignored otherwise. Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Example: 2020-01-15.

params.name: type
params.doc: Creation type for creating a calendar year, if isCustom is not set. Either LATEST, which will create the next year after the latest existing year, or EARLIEST, which will create the year before the earliest existing year. Defaults to LATEST.

operations.title: List history
operations.doc: Returns the history list.

params.name: dir
params.doc: The direction of the sort order (ascending or descending). Defaults to 'DESC'.

params.name: filter
params.doc: An array of filters to filter the list. All filters must match (AND). This is a JSON array [{...},{...},...] with the following parameters:

sub.name: comparison
sub.doc: Comparison type. Defaults to 'like'.

sub.name: field
sub.doc: The name of the column to filter by.

sub.name: value
sub.doc: Text to filter by, or a JSON array of multiple values (OR).

params.name: limit
params.doc: The number of entries to retrieve. Defaults to 100.

params.name: orderId
params.doc: ID of order to retrieve the history for. See Order.

params.name: personId
params.doc: ID of person to retrieve the history for. See Person.

params.name: query
params.doc: Fulltext search query.

params.name: start
params.doc: The starting entry. Defaults to 0.

params.name: statementId
params.doc: ID of salary statement to retrieve the history for. See Salary statement.

operations.title: Categorize articles
operations.doc: Assigns one or multiple articles to the desired category. Returns either a success or error message.

params.name: ids
params.doc: The IDs of the entries to categorize, comma-separated.

params.name: target
params.doc: The ID of the target category.

operations.title: Create category
operations.doc: Creates a new category. Returns either a success or multiple error messages (for each issue).

params.name: name
params.doc: The name of the category. This can contain localized text. To add values in multiple languages, use the XML format like this: <values><de>German text</de><en>English text</en></values>

params.name: allocations
params.doc: Allocations to cost centers for all articles in this category. These will be used in order items, when selecting the article. If allocations are set here, they override any allocations that would be automatically made by the corresponding sales/purchase account. This is a JSON array [{...},{...},...] with the following parameters:

sub.name: share
sub.doc: Allocation share. For example, if you have two cost centers, and one has a share of 3, and the other has a share of 1, then the amount is allocated 3:1 (which equals 75% to 25%).

sub.name: toCostCenterId
sub.doc: ID of cost center to allocate to. See Cost center.

params.name: parentId
params.doc: The ID of the parent category.

params.name: purchaseAccountId
params.doc: The ID of the purchase account, which will be used when purchasing articles in this category through Orders.

params.name: salesAccountId
params.doc: The ID of the sales account, which will be used when selling aticles in this category through Orders.

params.name: sequenceNrId
params.doc: The ID of the sequence number used for services in this category. If empty, the sequence number of the parent category is inherited.

operations.title: Delete categories
operations.doc: Deletes one or multiple existing categories. Note that you can only delete empty categories. Returns either a success or error message.

params.name: ids
params.doc: The IDs of the selected entries, comma-separated.

operations.title: List categories
operations.doc: Returns a list of all categories.

operations.title: Read category
operations.doc: Returns a single category by ID.

params.name: id
params.doc: The ID of the entry.

operations.title: Get tree of categories
operations.doc: Returns a tree of all categories or the tree below a parent category.

params.name: id
params.doc: Optional ID of the parent category (omit to get all categories).

operations.title: Update category

params.doc: The ID of the category to update.

params.name: name

params.name: allocations
params.doc: Allocations to cost centers for all articles in this category. These will be used in order items, when selecting the article. If allocations are set here, they override any allocations that would be automatically made by the corresponding sales/purchase account. This is a JSON array [{...},{...},...] with the following parameters:

sub.name: share

sub.name: toCostCenterId

params.doc: The ID of the parent category.

params.name: purchaseAccountId
params.doc: The ID of the purchase account, which will be used when purchasing articles in this category through Orders.

params.name: salesAccountId
params.doc: The ID of the sales account, which will be used when selling aticles in this category through Orders.

params.name: sequenceNrId
params.doc: The ID of the sequence number used for services in this category. If empty, the sequence number of the parent category is inherited.

operations.title: Create article
operations.doc: Creates a new article. Returns either a success or multiple error messages (for each issue).

params.name: name
params.doc: The name of the article. This can contain localized text. To add values in multiple languages, use the XML format like this: <values><de>German text</de><en>English text</en></values>

params.name: attachments
params.doc: List of files to attach. This is a JSON array [{...},{...},...] with the following parameters:

sub.name: fileId
sub.doc: ID of the file to attach. See File.

params.name: binLocation
params.doc: The place within the building (e.g. A15, B04, C11, etc.) to locate the article. See locationId. isStockArticle must be true, ignored otherwise.

params.name: categoryId
params.doc: The ID of the category. See Article category.

params.name: currencyId
params.doc: The ID of the currency. Leave empty to use the default currency. See Currency.

params.name: custom
params.doc: Custom field values. They are stored as XML in this parameter. Example: <values><customField1>My value</customField1><customField2>["value 1","value 2"]</customField2></values>. Look up custom field variable names (e.g. "customField1") in the Custom fields API.

params.name: description
params.doc: A description of the article. This can contain localized text. To add values in multiple languages, use the XML format like this: <values><de>German text</de><en>English text</en></values>

params.name: isInactive
params.doc: Mark the article as inactive. The article will be greyed out. Defaults to false.

params.name: isPurchasePriceGross
params.doc: The purchase price is net (excluding tax) by default. This defines the purchase price as gross (including tax). Defaults to false.

params.name: isSalesPriceGross
params.doc: The sales price is net (excluding tax) by default. This defines the sales price as gross (including tax). Defaults to false.

params.name: isStockArticle
params.doc: Whether the article has a stock, i.e. the stock should be tracked and updated via sales and purchase orders. Defaults to false.

params.name: lastPurchasePrice
params.doc: The last purchase price of the article. Net (excluding tax) by default, see isPurchasePriceGross. This price is automatically updated by purchase orders.

params.name: locationId
params.doc: The ID of the location where the article can be found (e.g. a warehouse). See Location. Note that this represents the building whereas the binLocation parameter represents the place within the building. isStockArticle must be true, ignored otherwise.

params.name: maxStock
params.doc: The desired maximum stock of the article. isStockArticle must be true, ignored otherwise.

params.name: minStock
params.doc: The desired minimum stock of the article. isStockArticle must be true, ignored otherwise.

params.name: notes
params.doc: Some optional notes. This can contain limited HTML for styling. Allowed tags: a, p, div, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, ul, ol, li, blockquote, b, i, s, u, o, sup, sub, ins, del, strong, strike, tt, code, big, small, br, span, em. Allowed inline CSS rules: background, background-color, color, font, font-size, font-weight, font-style, text-align, text-indent, text-decoration.

params.name: nr
params.doc: The article number. Leave empty to generate the number with sequenceNumberId.

params.name: salesPrice
params.doc: The sales price of the article. Net (excluding tax) by default, see isSalesPriceGross.

params.name: sequenceNumberId
params.doc: The ID of the sequence number used to generate the article number (see nr). If this is empty, the sequence number will not update when nr is set. See Sequence number.

params.name: stock
params.doc: The current stock of the article. isStockArticle must be true, ignored otherwise.

params.name: unitId
params.doc: The ID of the unit (like pcs., meters, liters, etc.). See Units.

params.doc: Mark the article as inactive. The article will be greyed out. Defaults to false.

params.doc: The purchase price is net (excluding tax) by default. This defines the purchase price as gross (including tax). Defaults to false.

params.doc: The sales price is net (excluding tax) by default. This defines the sales price as gross (including tax). Defaults to false.

params.doc: Whether the article has a stock, i.e. the stock should be tracked and updated via sales and purchase orders. Defaults to false.

params.name: minStock
params.doc: The desired minimum stock of the article. isStockArticle must be true, ignored otherwise.

Allowed tags: a, p, div, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, ul, ol, li, blockquote, b, i, s, u, o, sup, sub, ins, del, strong, strike, tt, code, big, small, br, span, em. params.doc: Allocations to cost centers. This is a JSON array [{...},{...},...] with the following parameters:

sub.name: share
sub.doc: Allocation share. For example, if you have two cost centers, and one has a share of 3, and the other has a share of 1, then the amount is allocated 3:1 (which equals 75% to 25%).

sub.name: toCostCenterId
sub.doc: ID of cost center to allocate to. See Cost center.

params.doc: The exchange rate from foreign currency to main currency. Only required if the currency is not supported or if you want to use a different rate than suggested.

params.doc: Custom field values. They are stored as XML in this parameter. Example: <values><customField1>My value</customField1><customField2>["value 1","value 2"]</customField2></values>. Look up custom field variable names (e.g. "customField1") in the Custom fields API.

params.doc: The next book entry will be created X days before the start date. Leave empty or set to 0 to have the next book entry created on the start date itself. See recurrence parameter.

params.doc: The end date for the recurrence. Orders repeat automatically up until this date, when the recurrence will stop. Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Example: 2020-01-15.

sub.name: accountId

params.doc: Custom field values. They are stored as XML in this parameter. Example: <values><customField1>My value</customField1><customField2>["value 1","value 2"]</customField2></values>. Look up custom field variable names (e.g. "customField1") in the Custom fields API.

params.name: dateAdded
params.doc: The date of the book entry. Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Example: 2020-01-15.

params.name: daysBefore
params.doc: The next book entry will be created X days before the start date. Leave empty or set to 0 to have the next book entry created on the start date itself. See recurrence parameter.

params.name: endDate
params.doc: The end date for the recurrence. Orders repeat automatically up until this date, when the recurrence will stop. Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Example: 2020-01-15.

params.doc: Items for the collective book entry (Sammelbuchung). Omit to create a regular book entry, and set if you want to create a collective book entry. This is a JSON array [{...},{...},...] with the following parameters:

sub.name: accountId
sub.doc: The ID of the account. See Account.

sub.name: allocations
sub.doc: Allocations to cost centers. This is a JSON array [{...},{...},...] with the following parameters:

sub.name: share
sub.doc: Allocation share. For example, if you have two cost centers, and one has a share of 3, and the other has a share of 1, then the amount is allocated 3:1 (which equals 75% to 25%).

sub.name: toCostCenterId
sub.doc: ID of cost center to allocate to. See Cost center.

sub.name: associateId
sub.doc: The ID of the business associate (person). Instead of an ID you can also create a new person on-the-fly by entering a name here. See Person.

sub.name: credit
sub.doc: The amount on the credit side. Either debit or credit must be set.

sub.name: debit
sub.doc: The amount on the debit side. Either debit or credit must be set.

sub.name: description
sub.doc: The description of the item.

sub.name: taxId
sub.doc: The ID of the tax code. See Tax codes.

params.name: notes
params.doc: Some optional notes. This can contain limited HTML for styling. Allowed tags: a, p, div, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, ul, ol, li, blockquote, b, i, s, u, o, sup, sub, ins, del, strong, strike, tt, code, big, small, br, span, em. params.name: notifyPersonId
params.doc: The ID of the person to send a notification to. See notifyType parameter.

params.doc: Whether or not to send a notification e-mail when book entries have been created. Leave empty to not send any notification.

params.name: notifyUserId
params.doc: The ID of the user to send a notification to. See notifyType parameter. Note: User must be in this organization.

operations.doc: Creates a new book entry. Returns either a success or multiple error messages (for each issue).

params.name: accountId
params.doc: The ID of the account (e.g. a bank account). This is the contra account to the account defined in the order category (typically the debtors or creditors account). See Account.

params.name: orderIds
params.doc: The IDs of one or multiple orders, comma-separated. See Order.

params.name: amount
params.doc: The amount of the book entry (e.g. 125.50). Leave empty to use open amount of order.

params.name: currencyId
params.doc: The ID of the currency. Leave empty to use the default currency. See Currency.

params.name: currencyRate
params.doc: The exchange rate from foreign currency to main currency. Only required if the currency is not supported or if you want to use a different rate than suggested.

params.name: date
params.doc: The date of the book entry. Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Example: 2020-01-15.

params.name: description
params.doc: The description of the book entry.

params.name: reference
params.doc: An optional reference / receipt for the book entry.

params.name: taxId
params.doc: The ID of the tax code. See Tax codes.

params.name: templateId
params.doc: The ID of the book entry template. The templates are defined in the order category. See Order category.

operations.title: Create category
operations.doc: Creates a new category. Returns either a success or multiple error messages (for each issue).

params.name: accountId
params.doc: The ID of the account, which is typically the debtors account for sales and the creditors account for purchase. See Account.

params.name: namePlural
params.doc: The plural name of the category (e.g. 'Invoices'). This can contain localized text. To add values in multiple languages, use the XML format like this: <values><de>German text</de><en>English text</en></values>

params.name: nameSingular
params.doc: The singular name of the category (e.g. 'Invoice'). This can contain localized text. To add values in multiple languages, use the XML format like this: <values><de>German text</de><en>English text</en></values>

params.name: status
params.doc: The status list (like 'Draft', 'Open', 'Paid', etc.) for this order category. At least one status must exist. This is a JSON array [{...},{...},...] with the following parameters:

sub.name: icon
sub.doc: The icon/color of the status.

sub.name: name
sub.doc: The name of the status. This can contain localized text. To add values in multiple languages, use the XML format like this: <values><de>German text</de><en>English text</en></values>

sub.name: actionId
sub.doc: An action associated with the status, i.e. what happens after I change the status to this? The action ID looks like this for example: CATEGORY_9. This would mean that another document of the order category with ID 9 will be created after changing to this status (CashCtrl asks the user first). The first part is either CATEGORY or BOOK_TEMPLATE. Then comes an underscore and the actual ID of the category or book template (e.g. BOOK_TEMPLATE_10).

sub.name: isAddStock
sub.doc: Whether inventory stock is added with this status. Note that when changing between two statuses that both have isAddStock set, it will only be added once, not twice. No matter how many times you change the status, it's only ever added once. Defaults to false.

sub.name: isBook
sub.doc: Whether journal book entries will be created with this status. For example, the invoice status 'Draft' will not create any book entries, but all the other status after that ('Open', 'Paid', etc.) will. Defaults to false.

sub.name: isClosed
sub.doc: Whether the status closes / completes the order object. This would be the case, for example, if an invoice has been fully paid. The effect is that the invoice is no longer due, even if past the due date (so no longer marked red). Defaults to false.

sub.name: isRemoveStock
sub.doc: Whether inventory stock is removed with this status. Note that when changing between two statuses that both have isRemoveStock set, it will only be removed once, not twice. No matter how many times you change the status, it's only ever removed once. Defaults to false.

params.name: addressType
params.doc: Which address of the recipient to use in the order document. Defaults to MAIN.

params.name: bookTemplates
params.doc: The book (entry) templates defined in this order category. An example of a book template for order categories would be the 'Payment' book template, which already has the appropriate bank account set, so that payments can be added with one click. This is a JSON array [{...},{...},...] with the following parameters:

sub.name: accountId
sub.doc: The ID of the account in this book template. This is typically a bank account in case of a payment template, and it's the contra account to the account set on the order (debtors or creditors account). See Account.

sub.name: name
sub.doc: A name / description of the book template, which will be used as the description for the actual book entry. Example: 'Payment'. This can contain localized text. To add values in multiple languages, use the XML format like this: <values><de>German text</de><en>English text</en></values>

sub.name: isAllowTax
sub.doc: Whether the actual book entry will allow setting a tax rate. This is to prevent the user from making a mistake (e.g. for payment book entries). Defaults to false.

sub.name: taxId
sub.doc: The ID of the tax code in this book template. This is only used if isAllowTax is true. For a payment book entry template you generally wouldn't allow setting a tax rate. See Tax codes.

params.name: bookType
params.doc: Whether the account (see accountId) is on the debit or credit side in the book entry. Defaults to DEBIT.

params.name: currencyId
params.doc: The ID of the currency used by default for order objects in this category. Leave empty to use the default currency. See Currency.

params.name: dueDays
params.doc: The due days used by default for order objects in this category. The order date + due days equals the due date.

params.name: fileId
params.doc: An optional PDF document whose pages are added at the end of the order document. Supported type: PDF. Max. size: 500KB. Use the File API to upload a file and then use the file ID here.

params.name: footerTemplateId
params.doc: The ID of the footer text used for order objects in this category.

params.name: hasDueDays
params.doc: Whether order objects in this category can have due days. The dueDays parameter is ignored if set to false. Defaults to false.

params.name: headerTemplateId
params.doc: The ID of the header text used for order objects in this category.

params.name: isDisplayItemGross
params.doc: Whether order item totals are displayed as gross (including tax) or net. Defaults to false.

params.name: isDisplayPrices
params.doc: Whether prices and totals are displayed on the document. For example a delivery note might not display prices, but an invoice does. Defaults to false.

params.name: isInactive
params.doc: Mark category as inactive. Inactive categories are no longer displayed, but the documents in the category are not deleted. Defaults to false.

params.name: isSwitchRecipient
params.doc: Switch recipient? By default your company is the sender and the client/vendor is the recipient. This flag switches sender and recipient. Defaults to false.

params.name: layoutId
params.doc: The ID of the layout used for order objects in this category. See Order layout.

params.name: mailSubject
params.doc: The mail subject (when sending the document via e-mail). Can contain variables.

params.name: mailTemplateId
params.doc: The ID of the mail text used for order objects in this category.

params.name: message
params.doc: A message for the payment recipient (included in the pain.001 xml file).

params.name: responsiblePersonId
params.doc: The ID of the responsible person (Sachbearbeiter) used for order objects in this category. See Person.

params.name: roundingId
params.doc: The ID of the rounding used for order objects in this category. See Rounding.

params.name: sentStatusId
params.doc: The ID of the status to automatically set when the order document is either sent by mail or downloaded. See status parameter. This can only be set if the category has already been saved, otherwise the status might not have an ID yet.

params.name: sequenceNrId
params.doc: The ID of the sequence number used for order objects in this category. See Sequence number.

params.name: type
params.doc: The type of category (sales orders or purchase orders). Defaults to SALES.

params.name: before
params.doc: Reorder before the target entry, after otherwise. Defaults to true.

params.name: type
params.doc: The type of category. Defaults to SALES.

params.doc: The ID of the status to automatically set when the order document is either sent by mail or downloaded. See status parameter. This can only be set if the category has already been saved, otherwise the status might not have an ID yet.

params.name: sequenceNrId
params.doc: The ID of the sequence number used for order objects in this category. See Sequence number.

params.name: type
params.doc: The type of category (sales orders or purchase orders). Defaults to SALES.

operations.title: Continue as
operations.doc: Continue an order as another order (e.g. continue an offer as an invoice). Returns either a success or multiple error messages (for each issue).

params.name: categoryId
params.doc: The ID of the target category.

params.name: ids
params.doc: The IDs of one or multiple orders to continue, comma-separated.

params.name: associateId
params.doc: The ID of the business partner (customer / vendor). Mandatory only if changing between sales and purchase order. See Person.

params.name: date
params.doc: The date of the order. Leave empty to use today. Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Example: 2020-01-15.

params.name: notes
params.doc: Some optional notes. This can contain limited HTML for styling. Allowed tags: a, p, div, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, ul, ol, li, blockquote, b, i, s, u, o, sup, sub, ins, del, strong, strike, tt, code, big, small, br, span, em. Allowed inline CSS rules: background, background-color, color, font, font-size, font-weight, font-style, text-align, text-indent, text-decoration.

params.name: statusId
params.doc: The ID of the status to set. Leave empty to use the first status in the list. See Order category.

operations.title: Create order
operations.doc: Creates a new order. Returns either a success or multiple error messages (for each issue).

params.name: associateId
params.doc: The IDs of one or multiple business partners (customers / vendors), comma-separated. If you enter multiple IDs it will create a separate document for each business partner. See Person.

params.name: categoryId
params.doc: The ID of the category. See Order category.

params.name: date
params.doc: The date of the order. Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Example: 2020-01-15.

params.name: accountId
params.doc: The ID of the account. Leave empty to use the account from the category. See Account.

params.name: attachments
params.doc: List of files to attach. This is a JSON array [{...},{...},...] with the following parameters:

sub.name: fileId
sub.doc: ID of the file to attach. See File.

params.name: currencyId
params.doc: The ID of the currency. Leave empty to use the default currency. See Currency.

params.name: currencyRate
params.doc: The exchange rate from foreign currency to main currency. Only required if the currency is not supported or if you want to use a different rate than suggested.

params.name: custom
params.doc: Custom field values. They are stored as XML in this parameter. Example: <values><customField1>My value</customField1><customField2>["value 1","value 2"]</customField2></values>. Look up custom field variable names (e.g. "customField1") in the Custom fields API.

params.name: daysBefore
params.doc: The next order will be created X days before the start date. Leave empty or set to 0 to have the next order created on the start date itself. See recurrence parameter.

params.name: description
params.doc: A description of the order document.

params.name: discountPercentage
params.doc: The discount percentage for the entire order (can be overriden in items).

params.name: dueDays
params.doc: The due days. Order date + due days = Due date (the date, when payment is due).

params.name: endDate
params.doc: The end date for the recurrence (see recurrence parameter). Orders repeat automatically up until this date, when the recurrence will stop. Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Example: 2020-01-15.

params.name: groupId
params.doc: The ID of the order group (dossier). Use this to include the order in a dossier with other orders that belong together (e.g. the offer, order confirmation, delivery note and invoice of the same order). This is overridden by previousId (if both are set).

params.name: isDisplayItemGross
params.doc: Whether to display item totals as gross (including tax). Defaults to false (net).

params.name: items
params.doc: The list of order items. This is a JSON array [{...},{...},...] with the following parameters:

sub.name: accountId
sub.doc: The ID of the account (revenue account for sales, expense account for purchase). See Account.

sub.name: name
sub.doc: The name of the item.

sub.name: unitPrice
sub.doc: The price of the item (for one unit).

sub.name: allocations
sub.doc: Allocations to cost centers. This is a JSON array [{...},{...},...] with the following parameters:

sub.name: share
sub.doc: Allocation share. For example, if you have two cost centers, and one has a share of 3, and the other has a share of 1, then the amount is allocated 3:1 (which equals 75% to 25%).

sub.name: toCostCenterId
sub.doc: ID of cost center to allocate to. See Cost center.

sub.name: articleNr
sub.doc: The article number.

sub.name: description
sub.doc: A description of the item.

sub.name: discountPercentage
sub.doc: Discount percentage for the item price.

sub.name: inventoryId
sub.doc: The ID of the inventory article. See Inventory.

sub.name: quantity
sub.doc: The amount of units of the item. Defaults to 1.

sub.name: taxId
sub.doc: The ID of the tax code. See Tax codes.

sub.name: type
sub.doc: The type of item. Defaults to ARTICLE.

sub.name: unitId
sub.doc: The ID of the unit (pcs., hours, etc.). See Units.

params.name: language
params.doc: The language of the document.

params.name: notes
params.doc: Some optional notes. This can contain limited HTML for styling. Allowed tags: a, p, div, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, ul, ol, li, blockquote, b, i, s, u, o, sup, sub, ins, del, strong, strike, tt, code, big, small, br, span, em. Allowed inline CSS rules: background, background-color, color, font, font-size, font-weight, font-style, text-align, text-indent, text-decoration.

params.name: notifyEmail
params.doc: The e-mail address to send a notification to. See notifyType parameter.

params.name: notifyPersonId
params.doc: The ID of the person to send a notification to. See notifyType parameter.

params.name: notifyType
params.doc: Whether to send a notification e-mail when orders have been created or not. Leave empty to not send any notification.

params.name: notifyUserId
params.doc: The ID of the user to send a notification to. See notifyType parameter. Note: User must be in this organization.

params.name: nr
params.doc: The order number (e.g. 'IN-2001015' for an invoice). Leave empty to generate the number with sequenceNumberId. This becomes mandatory if a sequence number is set neither here nor in the order category.

params.name: previousId
params.doc: The ID of the previous order from which this order is created (Next step / Continue as). The new order will be grouped with the previous order in a dossier. See also groupId. This will override groupId (if both are set).

params.name: recurrence
params.doc: The interval of how often the order should be automatically repeated. Leave empty to not repeat the order. See also startDate and endDate.

params.name: responsiblePersonId
params.doc: The ID of the responsible person (Sachbearbeiter). See Person.

params.name: roundingId
params.doc: The ID of the rounding to use for the grand total. See Rounding.

params.name: sequenceNumberId
params.doc: The ID of the sequence number used to generate the order number (see nr). If empty, the sequence number of the category is used (if set). See Sequence number.

params.name: startDate
params.doc: The start date for the recurrence (see recurrence parameter). This is the date when the order will be repeated next. Should probably be called nextDate instead. Format: YYYY-MM-DD. Example: 2020-01-15.

params.name: statusId
params.doc: The ID of the status to set. Leave empty to use the first status in the list. See Order category.

operations.title: Delete orders
operations.doc: Deletes one or multiple orders. Returns either a success or error message.

params.name: ids
params.doc: The IDs of the selected entries, comma-separated.

operations.title: Mail document
operations.doc: Sends a document per e-mail to the desired recipient(s).

params.name: mailFrom
params.doc: The sender / from e-mail address.

params.name: mailSubject
params.doc: The mail subject. Can contain variables.

params.name: mailText
params.doc: The mail text. Can contain variables. This can contain limited HTML for styling. Allowed tags: a, p, div, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, ul, ol, li, blockquote, b, i, s, u, o, sup, sub, ins, del, strong, strike, tt, code, big, small, br, span, em. Allowed inline CSS rules: background, background-color, color, font, font-size, font-weight, font-style, text-align, text-indent, text-decoration.

params.name: orderIds
params.doc: The IDs of the orders to send as mail, comma-separated. See Order.

params.name: isCopyToMe
params.doc: Send a copy to me? (the sender, see mailFrom)

params.name: mailBcc
params.doc: The BCC (blind carbon copy) e-mail address. You can enter multiple addresses comma-separated.

params.name: mailCc
params.doc: The CC (carbon copy) e-mail address. You can enter multiple addresses comma-separated.

params.name: mailTo
params.doc: The recipient e-mail address. You can enter multiple addresses comma-separated. Leave empty to use the default e-mail address of the business associate.

params.name: sentStatusId
params.doc: The ID of the status to set on the order after the mail has been sent. See Order category.

operations.title: Read document
operations.doc: Returns a single document by order ID.

params.name: id
params.doc: The ID of the order.

operations.title: Download PDF
operations.doc: Downloads one or multiple order documents in one PDF file.

params.name: ids
params.doc: The IDs of one or multiple orders, comma-separated.

operations.title: Download ZIP
operations.doc: Downloads one or multiple order documents in a ZIP file (one PDF for each document).

params.name: ids
params.doc: The IDs of one or multiple orders, comma-separated.

operations.title: Update document
operations.doc: Updates an existing document. To update the actual order object, see Order.

params.name: id
params.doc: The ID of the order to update. See Order.

params.name: customReference
params.doc: Custom Swiss QR reference or ISO-11649 reference which overrides the generated reference. Must be a valid reference. A Swiss QR reference can only be set, if a valid QR-IBAN is set, otherwise set an ISO-11649 reference.

params.name: fileId
params.doc: An optional PDF document whose pages are added at the end of the order document. Supported type: PDF. Max. size: 500KB. Use the File API to upload a file and then use the file ID here.

params.name: footer
params.doc: The text displayed below the items list on the document used by default for order objects in this category. This can contain limited HTML for styling. Allowed tags: a, p, div, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, ul, ol, li, blockquote, b, i, s, u, o, sup, sub, ins, del, strong, strike, tt, code, big, small, br, span, em. params.name: header

Allowed inline CSS rules: background, background-color, color, font, font-size, font-weight, font-style, text-align, text-indent, text-decoration.

params.name: isDisplayItemGross
params.doc: Whether order item totals are displayed as gross (including tax) or net. Defaults to false.

params.name: isFileReplacement
params.doc: Replace the generated order document with the attached PDF file? (see fileId)

params.name: language
params.doc: The language of the document.

params.name: layoutId
params.doc: The ID of the layout. See Order layout.

params.name: orgBankAccountId
params.doc: The ID of the organization's bank account. See Bank account.

params.name: orgLocationId
params.doc: The ID of the sender location. See Location.

params.name: recipientAddressId
params.doc: The ID of the recipient address (person address). See Person.

params.name: recipientBankAccountId
params.doc: The ID of the recipient's bank account.

operations.title: Read dossier

params.name: id
params.doc: The ID of the entry.

params.name: groupId
params.doc: The ID of the group.

params.name: ids
params.doc: The IDs of the orders to add/remove, comma-separated.

params.name: groupId
params.doc: The ID of the group.

params.doc: The IDs of the orders to add/remove, comma-separated.

operations.title: Create layout
operations.doc: Creates a new layout. Returns either a success or multiple error messages (for each issue).

params.name: name
params.doc: A name to describe and identify the layout.

params.name: elements
params.doc: List of elements containing HTML/CSS snippets for the different parts of the layout.

sub.doc: The layout element ID (e.g. HEADER, FOOTER, etc.).

sub.name: css
sub.doc: The CSS snippet.

sub.name: html
sub.doc: The HTML snippet.

params.name: footer
params.doc: The footer text, which is displayed at the bottom of the document. This can contain limited HTML for styling. Allowed tags: a, p, div, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, ul, ol, li, blockquote, b, i, s, u, o, sup, sub, ins, del, strong, strike, tt, code, big, small, br, span, em. params.name: isCountryEnglish
params.doc: Display country always in english (UPU standard)? Defaults to true.

params.name: isCountryUppercase
params.doc: Display country uppercase (UPU standard)? Defaults to true.

params.name: isDisplayDocumentName
params.doc: Display document name/title? Defaults to true.

params.name: isDisplayItemArticleNr
params.doc: Display article no. for items? Defaults to true.

params.name: isDisplayItemPriceRounded
params.doc: Display item prices rounded? Defaults to true.

params.name: isDisplayItemTax
params.doc: Display tax for items? Defaults to false.

params.name: isDisplayItemUnit
params.doc: Display unit for items? Defaults to true.

params.name: isDisplayLogo
params.doc: Display logo? Defaults to true.

params.name: isDisplayOrgAddressInWindow
params.doc: Display (your) organization address in window? Defaults to true.

params.name: isDisplayPageNr
params.doc: Display page numbers? Defaults to true.

params.name: isDisplayPayments
params.doc: Display payments? Defaults to true.

params.name: isDisplayPosNr
params.doc: Display item numbering? Defaults to true.

params.name: isDisplayRecipientNr
params.doc: Display recipient number (customer/vendor no.)? Defaults to true.

params.name: isDisplayResponsiblePerson
params.doc: Display responsible person (Sachbearbeiter)? Defaults to true.

params.name: isDisplayZeroTax
params.doc: Display zero tax (with a value of 0.00)? Defaults to false.

params.name: isInactive
params.doc: Mark the layout as inactive. Inactive layouts are greyed out and are no longer suggested.

params.name: isOmitSameCountry
params.doc: Omit country, if same between sender/recipient? Defaults to true.

params.name: isQrEmptyAmount

params.name: isQrNoLines

params.name: isQrNoReferenceNr
params.doc: Display QR invoice without reference number? Generates reference number by default.

params.name: letterPaperFileId

params.name: logoHeight
params.doc: The height of the logo in centimeters.

params.name: pageSize
params.doc: The page size of the document. Defaults to A4.

params.name: parentId
params.doc: The ID of the parent layout to inherit from. Letter paper, HTML and CSS will be inherited from the parent.

params.doc: The ID of the order category to filter by. See Order category.

params.name: columns
params.doc: The columns to include in the list, comma-separated. Check the list.json for available column names.

params.name: dir
params.doc: The direction of the sort order (ascending or descending). Defaults to 'DESC'.

params.name: filter
params.doc: An array of filters to filter the list. All filters must match (AND). This is a JSON array [{...},{...},...] with the following parameters:

sub.name: comparison
sub.doc: Comparison type. Defaults to 'like'.

sub.name: field
sub.doc: The name of the column to filter by.

sub.name: value
sub.doc: Text to filter by, or a JSON array of multiple values (OR).

params.name: fiscalPeriodId
params.doc: The ID of the fiscal period, from which we retrieve the orders.

params.name: groupId
params.doc: The ID of the order group (dossier) to filter by.

params.name: limit
params.doc: The number of entries to retrieve. Defaults to 100.

params.name: onlyCostCenters

params.name: onlyNotes
params.doc: Flag to only include entries with notes. Defaults to false.

params.name: onlyOpen
params.doc: Flag to only include open orders (incomplete status like 'Open' as opposed to completed status like 'Paid'). Defaults to false.

params.name: onlyOverdue
params.doc: Flag to only include orders that are overdue (past the due date). Defaults to false.

params.name: query
params.doc: Fulltext search query.

params.name: sort

params.name: start
params.doc: The starting entry. Defaults to 0.

params.name: statusId
params.doc: The ID of the order status to filter by.

params.name: type
params.doc: The type of order (sales or purchase).
